**WHY SPEKTR

**At spektr, we are on a mission to automate the world’s most complex compliance workflows through AI. Founded by the team behind HelloFlow (acquired by Trulioo), spektr is building the infrastructure and AI agents to run compliance at scale.

Compliance, built like product.

Financial services has changed enormously. Much of the technology behind compliance hasn’t. Teams still spend hours on manual checks, disconnected systems slow down launches, and entering a new market can mean rebuilding the same processes all over again.

We’re changing that. spektr gives regulated businesses one platform for onboarding, monitoring and investigations, with configurable workflows and AI agents that do the legwork. Product, Operations and Compliance can move together, with the control they need to grow.

It’s a huge opportunity in an industry that has moved slowly for too long. We’ve built a product we’re proud to put in front of the most demanding customers. Now we’re looking for people who want to help get it into their hands.

$26M raised, including a $20M Series A led by NEA, with backing from Northzone, Seedcamp and PreSeed Ventures.

Customers worth getting excited about. We work with businesses including Pleo, Trustly, Nexi and Santander. These are large accounts with complex problems, ambitious teams and plenty of room for us to make a difference.

Three offices: Copenhagen, London and Iași, with customers across more than 15 countries.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**We’re hiring a Product Owner to build products that compliance teams at banks and payment companies rely on every day, in more than 15 countries. You’ll work across the core of the spektr platform, from onboarding and monitoring to investigations, where our AI agents are taking on work that used to take analysts hours.

You will shape what compliance looks like when AI agents do most of the work. You’ll prototype, put ideas in front of compliance teams early, and work with engineering and design to ship what holds up in a regulated environment. You’ll do it at a Series A startup that moves fast, with the autonomy to take an idea from a blank page to a product running at banks and payment companies.

This is a chance to help define how compliance gets done, not to digitise the way it’s always been done.

**What You Will Be Doing

**

• Prototype fast and test with real users. Build working prototypes, often with AI tools, and put them in front of compliance and operations teams at banks and payment companies in days rather than months. Keep what works and drop what doesn’t.

• Explore several ways to solve a problem before committing to one, and come back with a clear view on which gives users the best experience, and why.

• Shape the product experience with our designers. Make complex compliance workflows simple to use, so analysts spend their time on decisions, not on the tool.

• Push how far AI can go in compliance. Our customers are regulated institutions, so every automated decision has to be explainable and defensible. You’ll work out what our AI agents can take on, what a human still needs to review, and what it takes for a compliance team to trust the result, then move that line further with each release.

• Turn customer requests into platform capabilities. When a customer asks for something specific, find the version that solves their problem and fits into the existing platform, so it stays configurable and works for the next customer too.

• Work hand in hand with engineering in Copenhagen and Iași. Align on what we’re building and why, agree how it fits the platform’s direction, and make the calls that keep work moving.

• Learn from the field. Work with our implementation team, who sit on site with customers and see every rough edge first, and use what they and our production data show you to decide what to improve.

**What We Are Looking For

**

• You’ve owned product on a B2B platform and can show us what you built, how you tested it with users and what changed as a result. Experience in financial services, fintech or another regulated industry is a plus.

• You build with AI. AI tools are part of how you prototype, research and explore ideas every day, and you have a view on how AI is changing the way products get made.

• Hands-on and fast. You’d rather show a working prototype than describe one, and you’re comfortable putting early work in front of users to learn quickly.

• Strong product and UX instincts. You can take a complex workflow and make it feel simple, and explain why one design works better than another.

• A platform thinker. When a customer asks for something, you look for the solution that fits the existing platform and scales beyond that one customer.

• Technical enough to go deep with engineers. You understand how systems, data and APIs fit together, and engineers want you in the room when decisions get made.

• Opinionated and open. You have a clear view on how things should work, argue for it, and change your mind when users or evidence show you otherwise.

• Close to customers by instinct. You’d rather sit in on a call with a bank’s onboarding team than read a summary of it.

Your route into product might have been through engineering, design, data, solutions architecture or operations. We’re interested in what you’ve built, how you think, and how quickly you learn. Prior compliance experience is a plus but isn’t a requirement.

**OUR PROCESS

**

• Intro call with our Talent team (30 minutes)

• Technical Interview (30 minutes)

• Technical Interview (60 minutes)

**How To Apply

**We hire the smartest, kindest, and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work. You’ll be joining a team with a proven track record and the "Product-Market Fit" to change an entire industry.

spektr is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, disability, sexual orientation or any other characteristic, and we assess every candidate against the same role requirements.

Are you passionate about renewable energy and eager to work at the forefront of the global energy transition? PEAK Wind is seeking a Structural Engineer Consultant to support Wind Turbine (WTG) and Balance of Plant (BoP) engineering on offshore wind projects, with a focus on Wind Turbine Components, jacket foundation design, scour and scour protection, and cable mechanical engineering.

Introducing the WTG & BoP Engineering Team

You will become part of our WTG & BoP Engineering team, where we work collaboratively to support renewable energy projects around the world. Our team consists of highly motivated professionals who bring diverse backgrounds and a strong commitment to excellence. We support one another, share knowledge, and celebrate both individual and collective achievements.

You will report to the Head of WTG & BoP Engineering and work closely with colleagues across different areas, bringing your perspective to a collaborative and purposeful team environment.

How You Will Make an Impact

As a Structural Engineer Consultant, you will contribute to the successful development, construction, and operation of our clients’ wind projects. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Supporting End of Warranties activities, technical due diligence, and asset management topics for clients throughout the development, construction, and operational phases of wind farms.

• Providing engineering expertise across both WTG and BoP systems, including turbine components, jacket foundations, scour protection, inter-array and export cables, offshore substations, and associated infrastructure.

• Leading the engineering activities related to foundation, scour protection, and cable work packages for offshore wind projects, from development and procurement through construction and into operations.

• Acting as a trusted technical advisor on jacket foundation design and scour management, reviewing foundation and scour protection solutions from design basis through detailed design, installation, and monitoring to ensure safe, robust, and cost-effective performance.

• Providing cable mechanical engineering support, including inter-array and export cable routing, burial and protection, cable protection systems, crossings, and the cable - foundation interface.

• Identifying, assessing, and mitigating technical risks related to turbine components, foundations, scour, cables, and asset integrity, and maintaining the project technical risk register.

• Following up on the certification process and managing interfaces with certification bodies to ensure that designs and deliverables meet the relevant standards and requirements.

• Contributing to the development of best practices and knowledge sharing across PEAK Wind’s offshore engineering services.

What Will Make You Successful in This Role

At PEAK Wind, we know success comes in many forms. What matters most is your mindset, curiosity, and drive to make an impact. The following qualities and experiences will help you succeed in this role:

• A degree in a relevant field such as Mechanical, Structural, Civil, Geotechnical, or Offshore Engineering, or similar.

• A minimum of 5 years post-education professional experience in offshore wind, the wider offshore industry, or another complex environment.

• Clear and effective communication skills in English, both spoken and written.

• A structured approach to problem-solving and the ability to take initiative.

• A collaborative mindset and the ability to thrive in an international, cross - functional team.

• Solid understanding of WTG components, including their function, common failure modes, and repair methodologies

• Solid understanding of the offshore wind foundation design process, particularly for jacket structures, including the impact of scour and the design of scour protection.

• Knowledge of subsea cable systems and cable mechanical engineering, such as burial and protection, cable protection systems, crossings, and the cable - foundation interface.

• Good knowledge of offshore wind EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction) as well as O&M (Operations and Maintenance), including how design and installation choices affect long - term operation of the asset.

• Familiarity with offshore wind industry standards and certification frameworks, such as DNV standards, IEC, IECRE, and Eurocodes.

Why Join PEAK Wind

• An international, inclusive, and diverse workplace where differences are valued

• The opportunity to work on leading renewable energy projects alongside experienced industry professionals

• Flexible working arrangements that support both your career and personal life

• A flat organisational structure where your ideas are welcomed and your contributions matter

• A strong focus on your learning, development, and professional growth

• A culture that values commitment, meaningful contributions, and having fun

Our Commitment to Inclusion and Fair Hiring

We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace drives innovation, creativity, and stronger results. At PEAK Wind, we are committed to fair and transparent hiring processes, welcoming candidates from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Our hiring decisions focus on what each person brings to the role and our team, and we are committed to ensuring transparent salary structures, with pay decisions based on clear, objective, and gender‑neutral criteria. Salary information, including the relevant salary band, will be shared with candidates when they are invited to a first interview.

How to Apply

We look forward to receiving your application. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the recruitment process once the right candidate has been found. Please apply directly through our website. If you have any questions or would like to know more about the position, please contact People & Development at recruitment@peak-wind.com.

About PEAK Wind

PEAK Wind is an independent renewable energy specialist in commercial, financial, and technical operations, delivering advisory, intelligence, and asset management services to investors and developers around the world. From onshore and offshore wind generation to Power-to-X, we work across the entire energy lifecycle to optimise operations and maintenance, enhance asset performance, and provide a holistic view of renewable infrastructure portfolios.

Our values - Expertise, Passion, Unity, and Integrity - are reflected in everything we do, from how we support our clients to how we collaborate as a team. At PEAK Wind, you will be able to apply your professional skills in a dynamic environment and experience a meaningful responsibility and involvement.

**Spirii is looking for an Engineering Manager!

**If you are passionate about cutting-edge software development technologies, leading agile teams, the EV industry, and creating outstanding products, join Spirii’s fantastic growth journey to lead the way for a sustainable future.

**The Job

**Spirii develops and provides world-class charging products and digital solutions to customers with electric cars. Our Digital Development department is proud to drive a listen, learn, and lead culture that allows us to constantly improve our ways of working. As Engineering Manager, you lead 1-2 of our engineering teams of 6–12 engineers and are accountable for making it a high-performing team. You own the people, the health of the team and the soundness of its engineering. You do this through others: Tech Leads and Senior Engineers guide the technical work day-to-day, and you make sure good decisions get made, quality stays high, and the team keeps getting better.

Spirii is adopting agentic development as the way we build software. AI agents are becoming part of how our engineers design, code, test, review and operate systems. You'll make it real in your team, working with colleagues across engineering to shape how we do it.

You work very closely with a Product Manager and a Designer. Product owns what we build and why; you own how well the team delivers it. You report to the Head of Engineering.

**What You Will Do

****Lead and grow your people

**

• Own the full people cycle for your team: hiring, onboarding, one-on-ones, feedback, career development, performance reviews and handling underperformance early and fairly.

• Build a team where people trust each other, take ownership and do their best work at a sustainable pace.

• Help your engineers grow, including senior engineers stepping into technical leadership.

**Own team performance

**

• Be accountable for the team's delivery, predictability and quality, and for how it improves over time.

• Define with Product what good looks like, and track it with evidence such as delivery flow, reliability, and team health, not gut feeling.

• Turn priorities into clear commitments, make trade-offs visible, and protect the team so committed work gets finished.

**Lead the shift to agentic development in your team

**

• Make agentic development part of how your team works every day, moving beyond individual experiments to shared practice.

• Adapt how work flows through your team as agents take on more of the building. That includes how work is specified, how code is reviewed and how quality is assured.

• Apply shared practices for quality, security and data handling as they develop, and stay accountable for what your team ships.

• Work with colleagues across engineering on how we adopt agentic development. Bring your team's needs and feedback, and help test and roll out new tools and practices.

• Track what agentic development changes for your team's delivery and quality, and share what you learn with other teams.

**Ensure sound engineering

**

• Be accountable for the quality of your team's engineering decisions, including architecture, security, operational readiness, observability and technical debt, while your Tech Lead and engineers lead the design work.

• Make sure what the team ships is tested, observable and ready to run in production, and that incidents lead to real learning.

• Work with other Engineering Managers and Tech Leads to keep our platform and practices coherent across teams.

**Collaborate across Spirii

**

• Partner with Product, Design, other departments and external consultants to align priorities and resolve dependencies.

• Communicate clearly and early about progress, risks and trade-offs.

**Who You Are

**

• You care about people and want to build teams that grow, thrive and deliver.

• You hold a high bar for quality and for yourself, and you take ownership of results.

• You're genuinely excited about AI as the new way to build software. You want to be ahead of the curve, and you're curious about where it goes next.

• You're technical enough to challenge a design, read an incident and spot risk, even if you're not writing production code day to day.

• You communicate clearly with engineers, product people and leadership alike.

**Qualifications

**The ideal candidate has relevant experience with development of digital cloud-based solutions in an agile start-up environment and can take the responsibility for leading a team of developers.

We further look for a candidate with the following experience and personal traits:

• Relevant technical graduate degree at minimum bachelor level (engineer).

• 3+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager with direct reports, including hiring, coaching and performance management.

• A background as a software engineer (backend or full-stack) building cloud-based solutions.

• Solid understanding of distributed systems, such as microservices and APIs, and what it takes to run them reliably in production.

• Experience improving engineering practices like automated testing, CI/CD, observability or incident management.

• Familiarity with DORA metrics or similar ways of measuring delivery.

• Experience making senior engineers and tech leads more effective, rather than doing their work for them.

**It's an advantage if you have

**

• Experience leading a team's adoption of AI-assisted or agentic development, including changing practices, not just introducing tools.

• Experience with AWS and containerised workloads.

• Experience from eMobility products.

• Experience leading a team through organisational change.

The position is a permanent position in Copenhagen, Denmark. Danish language is not a requirement, but Fluent English language skills are required.

**Benefits

**It is important for us to create a healthy, diverse, fun, and creative working environment, so besides all the basic benefits, we also focus a lot on social activities, flexible working hours and a good work life balance.

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance.

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most.

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry.

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office.

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii gym

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects.

• Two innovation days per month for YOU to choose what you work on.

The position is a permanent position in Copenhagen, Denmark. Danish language is not a requirement, but Fluent English language skills are required.

**About Spirii – Who We Are

**Spirii is a full-service e-mobility provider which offers hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and the public sector. Spirii was founded seven years ago as a company. Nevertheless, the people in Spirii have extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, as well as the development of future transport- and energy systems.

Spirii is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences. Spirii strives to create an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, race, sexual/religious orientation, or disability.

Senior Gameplay Programmer on WHAT THE CAR?

Do you love working in small, creative teams turning wild ideas into a reality? What about having creative and technical ownership from ideation through to release? Read on!

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

WHAT THE CAR? is our absurdly silly racing adventure game which addresses fundamental questions such as… What if a car had legs? Or a jetpack? Or secretly identified as a sailboat? First launched in 2023 on Apple Arcade and now also on Steam, it has gained a steady following of dedicated fans who have contributed hundreds of thousands of community-built levels.

We’re looking for a Senior Gameplay Programmer to help us continue to build upon CAR’s success by expanding upon its absurdly silly universe! We believe the best people to come up with ideas are the ones implementing them, so we expect a high degree of creativity and game design knowledge from our Gameplay Programmers, in addition to their crazy tech skills. This role involves around 60% programming and 40% game design.

**Here’s What That Looks Like Day To Day

**

• Build and ship gameplay code. You’ll implement features end-to-end in an existing Unity/C# codebase and ship regularly in a live environment.

• Generate design ideas. You’ll take part in shaping features, articulate intent, evaluate tradeoffs, and iterate through discussion with the team.

• Keep the game healthy. Fix bugs, improve systems, review test videos, and document findings so issues don’t come back to haunt us.

• Extend and refine what’s there. You’ll build on existing mechanics, making them more robust and enjoyable for players.

• Support and collaborate. You’re part of a small, closely knit, cross discipline team where people help each other reach their goals.

• Prototype and let go. Not everything ships, and that’s fine. Comfort with iteration and refactoring is part of the job.

**You’re a great match if

**

• You have 8+ years of commercial game development experience, having shipped at least two games as part of a team

• You have strong Unity and C# skills. You’re comfortable navigating a shared codebase and writing maintainable code you’d be proud to hand off

• You care about stability, performance, and long-term maintainability, and you leave systems better than you found them

• You genuinely value collaboration and working very closely with every member of the team

• You approach other people’s ideas with openness and try to understand the intention before giving feedback or pushing back

**Nice to have

**

• Experience working on live games

**Requirements For Any Job At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership - you spot problems, design and implement creative solutions that push projects forward

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness, and creativity, and you actively contribute to sustaining that culture

• You value a positive work environment

• You contribute to making the studio a fun and supportive place

**Practicalities

**

• Primarily work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen

• Only open to candidates who are already eligible to work in Denmark as we don’t offer relocation support or visa sponsorship for this role

• 37-hour work week, with flexible work hours

• No crunch, we put people before deadlines

• Our working language is English

**We offer

**

• Silly but ambitious projects

• The chance to contribute to great games that reach millions of players

• A playful and ambitious work environment where experimentation is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights and team events

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant just a walk across the lakes away, with plant-based options (and soft ice on Thursdays).

• Six weeks of paid vacation

• Paid parental leave at full salary for the periods covered by state reimbursement

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked

• Pension plan and private health insurance

• Endless amounts of coffee

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, which is played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 50 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make everyone laugh. To do so, we focus on exploring comedy through gameplay. We like to break player expectations, use wonderful music, slick art, and create a quirky atmosphere. We experiment a lot, and it doesn’t always work out, but we always learn something.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games - and we believe diversity makes for better teams. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and will challenge us and our way of doing things.

Do you enjoy turning complex business questions into clear insights and practical recommendations?

Scan Global Logistics is looking for a Strategy Analyst to join our Group Transformation team.

This is an opportunity for someone early in their career who wants to work close to senior management and gain exposure to strategic priorities, business performance and transformation initiatives across a global organisation.

You do not need to have all the answers from day one. What matters is that you are analytical, curious, commercially minded and comfortable getting into the detail.

What you can expect

• You will join a global business with significant ambitions and an active transformation agenda.

• Broad exposure across the organisation and the opportunity to work closely with experienced leaders on real business challenges.

• For the right person, we expect the scope and responsibility to grow quickly. This is a strong opportunity to build a career within strategy, transformation or general business leadership.

• A straightforward, collaborative environment where you can challenge the status quo while staying focused on getting things done.

The role

As Strategy Analyst, you will support strategic and transformation initiatives across Scan Global Logistics.

You will work with data, business cases and management information, but the role is broader than pure financial analysis. You will help us understand business problems, identify opportunities, structure decisions and follow initiatives from idea through implementation.

Your work could range from analysing the performance of a business area or testing the assumptions behind an investment case to supporting a major transformation programme or preparing material for senior management.

In short, you will help turn data and complexity into decisions and action.

Your key responsibilities

• Analyse business performance, operational data and strategic opportunities

• Build financial models, business cases and scenario analyses

• Support strategic and transformation projects across functions and geographies

• Help structure complex or ambiguous business questions

• Track progress, value creation and key performance indicators

• Prepare clear decision material and presentations for senior management

• Work with colleagues across Finance, Operations, Commercial, our Regions and other functions

• Challenge assumptions and help ensure decisions are based on facts

• Support implementation and follow-up when initiatives move from analysis into execution

• Contribute to ad hoc strategic analyses and projects for senior management

Who are we looking for?

You probably have 1–4 years of relevant experience, although we are more interested in your capabilities and potential than the exact number of years. Your background could be from:

• Management consulting

• Corporate strategy or business development

• FP&A or commercial finance

• Business intelligence or analytics

• Transaction services

• A graduate programme or similar analytical role

You may also be a strong recent graduate with relevant internships and an excellent analytical foundation.

We imagine you have a degree within business, economics, finance, engineering or another analytical discipline.

What matters most

We are looking for someone who:

• Is genuinely strong with numbers and analytical problem-solving

• Can structure a problem before jumping to the answer

• Is comfortable working in Excel and PowerPoint

• Is curious about how a business actually works

• Can translate analysis into a clear recommendation

• Is pragmatic and willing to get into the detail

• Communicates clearly and simply

• Takes ownership and follows things through

• Is comfortable working with different stakeholders and cultures

• Wants to learn quickly and take on increasing responsibility

Experience from the logistics industry is not required but would be a plus. We focus on finding someone with the right analytical ability, curiosity and drive.

Why join Scan Global Logistics?

At SGL, you will join an international logistics company with an entrepreneurial culture, high ambitions and a strong belief that results are created by people who take responsibility. Our DNA is built on Respect, Integrity, Entrepreneurship & Fun.

At Scan Global Logistics, we value people who are straightforward, collaborative and willing to challenge the status quo while staying focused on getting things done.

Interested?

Send your CV and application through the SGL career portal. We review applications on an ongoing basis and will close the process when the right candidate has been found.

For further information, please contact Nikolaj Lei Jacobsen, Global CTO, on +45 4332 4641 or visit

www.scangl.com.

Are you passionate about connecting digital strategy with hands-on execution to drive measurable marketing impact across European markets?

As our new Digital Marketing Manager, Western Europe, you'll shape and deliver the regional digital marketing agenda across 16 Western European markets, combining strategic direction with hands-on activation that strengthens customer engagement, lead generation, and conversion.

What you will be doing

As a key member of the Western Europe Marketing team, you'll create impact by translating business priorities into connected, measurable digital experiences that drive customer engagement and marketing effectiveness across one of Grundfos' most important regions.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Set and drive the digital marketing direction for Western Europe across 16 markets, translating regional business priorities into a clear digital roadmap aligned with global platforms, frameworks and best practices.

• Plan, execute and optimise multi-channel digital campaigns across websites, email, social media and search, aligned with regional priorities and customer journeys.

• Drive web performance and local optimisation across Western Europe, including SEO/GEO, traffic development and digital customer journeys, identifying opportunities to improve discovery, engagement and conversion.

• Track, analyse and report on digital performance, campaign ROI and KPIs, using A/B testing and performance insights to identify trends and deliver actionable optimisation recommendations.

• Support marketing technology adoption, automation, lead scoring, nurturing workflows and CRM integration to improve lead quality, conversion and alignment with Sales.

• Identify and translate emerging digital trends, including AI-driven discovery and changing search behaviour, into opportunities, while building digital capabilities and supporting execution across local teams.

What makes you a great fit

Above all, you're a strategic yet hands-on digital marketing professional who thrives at the intersection of planning and execution, with strong stakeholder management skills and a passion for turning data into better customer experiences. We'd also imagine that you have:

• 5+ years of experience in digital marketing roles covering strategy, campaign activation, and performance optimisation across multiple markets or regions.

• Hands-on expertise across the digital ecosystem, including web/CMS, SEO, paid media, marketing automation (e.g. Marketo), analytics, and lead management.

• Experience working in international matrix organisations, enabling collaboration across global, regional, and local teams.

• A strong analytical mindset with the ability to translate performance data into clear actions and priorities.

Why you'll love working here

Day to day, you can look forward to:

• A working environment built around your needs, with flexible hours, home working opportunities and parental support.

• Annual bonuses, health insurance and a strong focus on well-being activities.

• Three days' additional paid leave for volunteering.

• On-demand training and structured development programmes to support your growth.

About Grundfos

Grundfos is one of the world’s leading water technology companies with more than 19.000 employees in 60+ countries all over the world. Our skills commit us to pioneering solutions to the world’s water and climate challenges and improve the quality of life for people. We dare to do things that others cannot or dare not do, as we believe innovation is not only a business opportunity, but an obligation. And what really matters to us is not short term profit, but the impact we make. By becoming part of our united powerful team, you too can drive this change no matter your role.

An inclusive team

We believe that the key to a work environment, where employees thrive and grow, is our ability to celebrate and value our differences in background, experiences and perspectives. In our recruitment process we welcome all professional people without consideration of age, colour, gender identity, national origin, physical or mental disability, ethnicity or religion.

Take technical ownership of our launched medical devices – driving product improvements, resolving technical challenges and ensuring long-term product performance.

Can you combine strong engineering judgement with hands-on technical work, take ownership of product design challenges and drive solutions through to completion?

Qufora develops intuitive medical devices that help people with chronic bowel disorders live a more fulfilled life. We are looking for an experienced Technical Product Owner to take technical responsibility for our launched products and help ensure their continued safety, performance and compliance.

Based at our headquarters in Allerød, north of Copenhagen, you will join our R&D organisation and work closely with colleagues across R&D, Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs and Commercial, as well as external manufacturing partners.

Your role

As Technical Product Owner (TPO), you will have overall technical responsibility for the design of assigned launched products, including packaging and labelling. You will maintain a clear overview of their design status, performance, quality and technical documentation throughout their lifecycle.

This is a hands-on engineering role where you combine technical ownership with practical problem-solving. You will carry out technical work yourself where appropriate and involve specialists when their expertise is needed.

For smaller, straightforward changes, you will manage the activities yourself. For larger or more complex initiatives, a Project Manager will support planning and cross-functional coordination, while you retain responsibility for the technical scope and execution.

Your key responsibilities

• Maintain technical product ownership: Take over product knowledge and documentation from development and keep product requirements, specifications, risk assessments and design documentation up to date.

• Monitor product performance: Evaluate feedback from complaints, post-market surveillance and production data to identify technical issues, risks and opportunities for improvement.

• Investigate and resolve technical issues: Lead technical investigations and apply Structured Problem Solving, including root cause analysis, to address product failures and design-related quality issues.

• Drive product design changes: Assess technical impacts, initiate and manage Change Requests (CRs) and Change Orders (COs), and ensure that required design changes and documentation updates are completed.

• Plan and execute verification: Define acceptance criteria, plan verification activities, perform selected tests and analyse and document results, involving relevant specialists as needed.

• Ensure continued design compliance: Assess the technical impact of new standards, regulatory requirements and product changes, and ensure that necessary technical actions and documentation are completed.

• Drive product improvements: Identify and implement design improvements that strengthen product performance, quality, manufacturability, supply reliability or cost efficiency.

Your experience and qualifications

• A relevant degree in engineering or a related technical discipline, with minimum 5 years of experience in medical device development or medical device lifecycle management.

• Practical experience with design control, change control, risk management and technical documentation within an ISO 13485 quality management system.

jobs.description:
Are you an experimental physicist eager to push light–matter interaction to its extremes? 

We offer a PhD scholarship at DTU Electro, where you will trap light in nanoscale optical cavities coupled to highly nonlinear 2D materials, and control them to let light interact with light far more strongly than conventional devices allow.

To trap and release light on demand, we use photonic crystal cavities in thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), whose strong electro-optic effect allows fast electrical control. Our team has recently demonstrated ultracompact TFLN cavities used as modulators [1], with electrically controllable coupling to waveguides [2], and as multiport switches [3]. The project builds on these results and shares fabrication efforts with our collaborators at Harvard University, who pioneered the TFLN platform [4].

Photons interact only through a material nonlinearity, and in conventional static cavities the interaction time is fundamentally bounded, which dynamically coupled cavities can overcome [5]. You will combine such cavities with atomically thin 2D semiconductors with exceptionally strong nonlinearities to explore a largely uncharted dynamic regime of nonlinear optics, aiming to generate quantum states of light, such as squeezed light, at ultralow energies. The project is part of the Center for Nanophotonics (NanoPhoton), a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will drive the experimental work in the project from device design to demonstration, working closely with PhD students, postdocs, and senior researchers at DTU and our collaborators at Harvard University. Depending on your interests, you will have the opportunity to:

• Design photonic crystal cavities and circuits using electromagnetic and multiphysics simulations.
• Fabricate devices in DTU Nanolab’s state-of-the-art cleanroom.
• Integrate 2D materials with photonic chips.
• Characterize devices using high-speed electro-optic, pulsed-laser, and quantum-optical measurements.
• Compare your experiments with theoretical models of cavity dynamics.
• Present your results at international conferences and in leading journals.
You are curious and driven, enjoy hands-on laboratory work, and take ownership of the progress and quality of your work.

Required qualifications:

• A strong background in optics or photonics.
• Experimental experience in optics or photonics, e.g., from your master’s project.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.
